newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian space center to launch 20 Western probes.
newsitem.headline: Russian space center to launch 20 Western probes.

text.p: Russia's top commercial satellite-launcher said Tuesday it planned to make eight Proton rocket launches in 1997, sending a total of 20 Western satellites into orbit.
Khrunichev Space Centre spokesman Sergei Zhiltsov said it planned the first commercial launch in May. "The Proton will carry the Telstar-5 communication satellite for AT&T Skynet," he said.
The centre also plans two Proton launches, each with seven Iridium satellites for Motorola Corp., in June and September, Ziltsov said.
He added that a Sky-1 satellite for MSI/News Corp. would also be launched in September.
In July the centre plans to launch the Pas-5 satellite for PanAmSat Co. and then in August and in October Astra-1G and Astra-2A probes for the Luxembourg-based SES agency.
The last launch is scheduled for December. The Russian-made booster will carry the Asiasat probe for Hongkong-based Asia Satellite Telecommunications, Zhiltsov said.
Six of the planned launches will be made by Khrunichev's U.S.-backed joint venture, International Launch Services, which was set up with Lockheed-Martin in 1993.
The Moscow-based Khrunichev centre produces Proton boosters and launches them from Baikonur cosmodrome in Kazakhstan.
